set.body:
Defect: D4 (remaps are arithmetic inside scorers with no provenance and no oracle: FilmFest +106, Friends 56->52, Sherlock 1000->50). Two review passes were needed to get the type right. Revision 2 used Maps vs MergedInto -- a class the AUTHOR asserts that the MAP determines (count of sources per target), so a constructor choice can disagree with the data and nothing catches the lie (rule 14). Then a third review found the laws still admitted a NON-bijection: {a -> To(x), b -> Removed} is total, injective on To, and covers x exactly once.

Do: SegmentRef(segmentation: SegmentationId, ordinal: Int) -- two ordinal spaces, two types. enum Target { To(ref, evidence: LinkEvidence); Removed(evidence) } -- ONE To, multiplicity COMPUTED. enum LinkClaim { Bijection, Coarsening, Edit } is what the constructor CHECKS, not a label. Name it LinkEvidence: `Evidence` collides with core.Evidence (claim.scala:29), which is spans-and-claims and the wrong shape.

Tests: Laws: Bijection admits ONLY To -- no Removed at all -- then enforce bijectivity. Coarsening: total, onto, no Removed, many-to-one by several To sharing a target (no 'survivor' selected, no sibling relabelled an editorial merge). Edit: total, every Removed evidenced. Plus two construction checks: every target's SegmentRef.segmentation == link.to; every map key is an ordinal of link.from (keys stay bare Int, tolerable only because the link names `from` -- ADR must say so). Composition is function composition on Option[SegmentRef]. The composability law as usually stated CANNOT pass: a composed target's LinkEvidence derives from two links while a declared a->c's is direct, so equality fails on the evidence field for EVERY witness -- compare modulo evidence, or add LinkEvidence.Composed(ab, bc).

Mutants (SD1 — each must die, recorded by name): drop the no-Removed rule from Bijection -> the {a->To(x), b->Removed} counterexample must fail. Accept a target whose segmentation != link.to -> that check must fail. Accept a Removed without evidence -> the evidence law must fail.

Exit: The five laws hold as discipline-munit suites over scalacheck generators (laws/CorpusGens.scala, CorpusLaws.scala, following the AddressGens/AddressableLaws convention).

Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-17-annotation-intake-contract.md S2 'Segmentations and links'
set.title: intake P3: SegmentLink -- To/Removed with computed multiplicity and a CHECKED LinkClaim
